title: RAJA Performance Suite: Performance Portability Analysis with Caliper and Thicket
problem: Benchmark codes lack comprehensive GPU programming model implementations needed to assess performance effects of code changes and hardware updates. Evaluating algorithmic and code changes across diverse architectures requires benchmarks covering multiple GPU programming models but most existing benchmarks do not.
motivation: Maintaining performant code across fast-evolving computer architectures and programming models is essential for scientific computing and requires effective benchmarking tools.
method: The RAJA Performance Suite includes computational kernels written in different GPU programming approaches. Using integrated Caliper and Thicket tools, it automatically identifies whether each kernel is limited by memory bandwidth or by processor computing speed (FLOPS—floating-point operations per second), then predicts performance on new hardware with different resource balances.
key_novelty: The key innovation is automatically detecting performance bottlenecks in code to predict how well it will perform on different hardware.
contributions: Comprehensive RAJA Performance Suite with computational kernels across multiple GPU programming models
Integration of Caliper and Thicket tools for systematic performance measurement and bottleneck analysis
Automated framework for classifying kernels by bottleneck type and predicting performance on new hardware
Empirical demonstration that memory-bound kernels benefit most from high-bandwidth memory while compute-bound kernels benefit from higher-FLOPS GPUs

metrics.speedup: Relative performance across GPU programming models and architectures
metrics.other: Memory bandwidth utilization, FLOPS efficiency, bottleneck characterization

limitations: Limitations and scope boundaries of the characterization methodology not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Performance portability benchmarking and bottleneck characterization
